title: unified-rollouts: proactive shadow+canary auto-rollback workflow
author: Aisha Verma
release_notes: Adds proactive auto-rollback workflow that combines shadow probing with staged canary traffic and metric-driven rollback policies. Includes observability metrics and e2e stability tests. Backwards-compatible config; no user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: incidents during recent canary rollouts showed that regressions visible only under shadow traffic or low-volume probing were not always caught before increasing live traffic. This PR implements a proactive auto-rollback workflow that runs shadow probing and lightweight canary stages with aggregated metric matching to reduce false positives while enabling fast automated rollback when real regressions are detected.

What I changed (summary):
- Implemented a new rollout controller path (proactive_shadow_canary) that sequences shadow probing -> staged canary -> ramp with automated rollback triggers.
- Added composite metric matching logic that combines latency P95, 5xx ratio, and model-quality signal (differences on golden prompts) for rollback decisions.
- Introduced stability guards and minimum-sample thresholds to avoid noisy rollback from small sample sizes.
- Instrumented new observability metrics and tracing spans for shadow probe sampling, canary ramp steps, and rollback decisions.
- Added e2e tests in perf-canary harness and unit tests for the rollback decision engine.
- Documentation: rollout strategy docs + config examples for operators (canary windows, probe weight, metric thresholds).

Checklist:
- [x] Controller implementation and unit tests
- [x] Observability & tracing metrics
- [x] E2E tests in perf-canary harness
- [x] Docs and upgrade notes
- [x] Backwards-compatibility: defaults match current rollout behavior when feature flag disabled

Notes on behavior and safety:
- The auto-rollback uses a composite score. Each metric has a configurable weight; default weights tuned conservatively.
- Rollbacks only occur after both threshold breach and minimum sample window to prevent flapping.
- There is an operator-facing emergency cutoff (manual abort API + Linear integration) to stop automated rollouts if needed.

Related: ENG-4583 for rollout design, SUP-7821 incident follow-up.

Testing performed:
- Local unit tests: new decision engine tests + existing rollout unit tests.
- Perf-canary: ran synthetic shadow probes and validated rollback trigger on injected regression.
- Integration: validated canary ramp and rollback with staging routing rules.

Migration/upgrade notes:
- New config keys under rollout.policy.proactive_shadow_canary. If absent, controller falls back to existing behavior.
- Operators with custom rollout policies should review thresholds after upgrade.

Contact: @aisha for follow-ups and rollout tuning.

review_comments: Marco Li: overall approach looks good. A few questions about the composite scoring weights — can we make defaults conservative and include an override in the UI?
Aisha Verma: replied: defaults are conservative (see docs) and the console exposes weight overrides per-rollout-policy. I've added a UI control and example configs.
Priya Nair: The minimum-sample threshold is crucial. Suggest adding a backoff window to prevent rapid toggles during high-error bursts.
Aisha Verma: added stability guards and backoff in controller loop; updated tests to assert no-flap behavior.
Devon Carter: e2e looked stable locally, but CI flaked on a timing-based test.
Aisha Verma: fixed by using deterministic clock in test harness and bumped timeout in e2e runner to accommodate CI VM variability.
